text: Almost every string is random in Kolmogorov's sense, yet no program can exhibit one. Is that a contradiction?
choices: Yes, and it shows Kolmogorov complexity is not a coherent definition.
No — the property is overwhelmingly common and individually unverifiable, which are compatible.
Yes, and it is resolved by noting that randomness is undefined for finite strings.
No, because 'almost every' means measure-theoretically, not for any actual string.
explanation: Pick a string at random and it is random with probability essentially 1; verify that any particular one is, and you cannot, ever. The two feel as though they should conflict and do not. It is the unit in miniature: the reachable part of a space can be vanishingly small and still be the only part you can work in.
